subject.title: Feature Request: User-Level Skill Preferences/Conventions Support

question: Should OpenClaw support a first-class per-skill user preference sidecar, and which contract should own it: markdown sidecar, structured `skills.entries.*.config`, or no core support?
rationale: The source evidence shows the requested behavior is not implemented, but adding it changes the public skill-loading and prompt-context contract rather than fixing a broken existing contract.

options.title: Standardize a markdown sidecar
options.body: Add a documented `preferences.md` or `conventions.md` sidecar that is loaded with the selected skill, versioned with the prompt snapshot, watched for refresh, and kept lower precedence than `SKILL.md`.

options.title: Use structured skill config only
options.body: Keep preferences under `skills.entries.*.config` and require each skill or plugin to interpret them, avoiding prompt-side markdown composition but leaving natural-language conventions less ergonomic.

options.title: Decline core support
options.body: Keep the current model where users either maintain a higher-precedence skill override, create a personal skill, or use global context files, and close this direction as not planned.

recommendation.title: Standardize a markdown sidecar
recommendation.body: Add a documented `preferences.md` or `conventions.md` sidecar that is loaded with the selected skill, versioned with the prompt snapshot, watched for refresh, and kept lower precedence than `SKILL.md`.

likelyOwner.reason: The current skill-loading contract, ClawHub skill flows, and docs history most strongly point to steipete for the product/API choice.
